lines.text: Hi, I'm Clawd! A very long time ago, people had no shops, no tools, and not even clothes. Just their hands, their brains, and each other.
Meet Koa and his friends. Their favourite thing? Racing through the corn, and playing chase until the sun goes down.
One hot day, Koa is hungry and thirsty. High up in a palm tree, he spots something round. Coconuts!
Koa hugs the trunk and starts to climb. Up a little, and whoops! Back down he slides.
He tries again, and again. Then he finds a trick. Grip with the feet, push, reach, and pull. Up, up, up!
At the top, he twists a coconut free. Thud! It lands in the sand.
Now for the hard part. Koa bites it. He squeezes it. He kicks it. Ow! Nothing. That shell is tough.
Then Koa has an idea. He picks up a heavy stone.
Bash! Bash! Crack! The coconut splits open, and there's sweet water inside.
A stone used to do a job is a tool. Humans and our ancestors have been making stone tools for more than three million years.
Koa shares with his friends. And that's how you open a coconut: try, fail, and try again!
See you in the next story!
